slides.heading: Truth Tables in Code
slides.body: Truth Tables in Code is part of Boolean Logic and Comparisons. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Truth Tables in Code
slides.body: A truth table shows how boolean operators behave for different True and False combinations. It helps you predict logic before coding.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: A truth table is like a checklist grid showing what happens for every possible pair of answers.

slides.heading: Example: Truth Tables in Code
slides.code:
a = True
b = False
print(a or b)

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Boolean expressions must produce True or False. Use comparisons and logical operators carefully.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Print the result of True and False.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Print the result of not (True or False).
